observation_summary: The application throws a NullPointerException when attempting to remove a marker from a CategoryPlot or XYPlot if no markers have been added to the specified layer/index, causing the markers list to be null.
hypothesis: The code assumes that the markers list retrieved from the map is never null. When no markers exist for a given index/layer, the map returns null, and calling .remove() on that null reference triggers a NullPointerException.
prediction: Adding a null check for the 'markers' variable before calling 'markers.remove(marker)' will prevent the NullPointerException and allow the method to return 'false' as expected when no marker is found.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows exactly this: an 'if (markers == null) { return false; }' block was added before the removal operation in both CategoryPlot and XYPlot, confirming that the missing validation of the 'markers' object was the root cause.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic missing guard/validation. The code attempts to perform an operation (remove) on an object (markers) without verifying if that object exists (is not null). This fits the definition of 'Checking' perfectly.
evidence_used: Stack trace shows NullPointerException at markers.remove(marker)
Fix diff adds 'if (markers == null) { return false; }' before the removal call

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The logic of the removal algorithm itself is correct; the issue is the lack of a guard against a null state.
